necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)—a condition that occurs 
primarily in premature infants or sick newborns, in which 
intestinal tissue dies; the cause for this disorder is unknown, 
but it is thought to be due to decreased blood ﬂ ow to the bowel, 
which keeps it from producing the normal protective mucus; if 
an infant is suspected of having necrotizing enterocolitis, feed-
ings are stopped to allow the bowel to rest
necrotizing fasciitis—inﬂ ammation of the connective tissue 
leading to necrosis of the tissue; may be caused by infection,
injury, or an autoimmune reaction
